thread:
amal: Hey folks — running `terraform plan` in staging after doing an import and plan is now proposing to RECREATE the managed identity resource. Not sure why, opened this thread for quick eyes :eyes:
jack: Can you paste the relevant snippet of the plan output?
amal: Sure, here's the block. I imported yesterday then ran plan: 
```
# module.app.module.identity.azuread_service_principal.sp will be created
+ resource "azuread_service_principal" "sp" {
+   application_id = "<computed>"
+   display_name   = "app-staging-sp"
+ }

# module.app.module.identity.azuread_service_principal.sp: Refreshing state... [id=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000]
```
jack: Hmm, the plan shows a create even though `state` has an id — that's odd. Did you import against the same resource address?
sanya: Also check which provider you imported with. We've had issues mixing `azurerm` and `azuread` providers. If the import used a different provider alias/state metadata, TF can think it's missing.
amal: I did `terraform import module.app.module.identity.azuread_service_principal.sp 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` from my laptop. I didn't set any explicit `-provider` flag.
oliver: If there are multiple provider instances (aliases) in the workspace, import might have attached the object to a different provider instance. Run `terraform state show module.app.module.identity.azuread_service_principal.sp` and check the provider field and principal_id.
amal: output from `terraform state show module.app.module.identity.azuread_service_principal.sp`:
```
# module.app.module.identity.azuread_service_principal.sp:
provider = "provider[\"registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/azurerm\"]"
principal_id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
application_id = "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111"
```
jack: Aha — state says provider is `azurerm`. But the resource block is `azuread_service_principal` which expects the `azuread` provider. That mismatch will cause TF to want to recreate.
sanya: Exactly. Two ways to fix: 1) move the state entry to the `azuread` provider with `terraform state replace-provider`/`terraform state mv` OR 2) re-import with `-provider=registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/azuread` so the entry is created with correct provider meta.
amal: Tried `terraform import -provider=registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/azuread module.app.module.identity.azuread_service_principal.sp 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` — plan still shows create.
oliver: After re-import, check `terraform state show` again. If the provider metadata on the state entry still points to azurerm, you can run: `terraform state replace-provider 'registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/azurerm' 'registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/azuread'` (with the exact provider addresses) in a safe branch. That updates the provider refs in state.
jack: Another safe path: `terraform state mv 'module.app.module.identity.azuread_service_principal.sp' 'module.app.module.identity.azuread_service_principal.sp' -state-out=tmp.tfstate` — basically copy to a temp state with the correct provider and then swap, but that's fiddly. `replace-provider` is designed for this.
amal: Quick question: will replace-provider affect other azurerm resources? We only want to touch the single SP.
sanya: `replace-provider` operates on provider type across state entries; if you map azurerm -> azuread globally, it will touch all entries that reference azurerm. So use `terraform state replace-provider -preserve-metadata` carefully and inspect with `terraform state list` beforehand. If you only have one wrong entry, `state mv` to a temporary address, edit the tfstate JSON and put back is safer but more manual.
amal: Ok. I ran `terraform state show` after the import and it still showed `provider = provider["registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/azurerm"]`. I'll try `state replace-provider` in a branch and run plan to verify.
jack: If you want, I can join and pair — I have bandwidth in ~20m. Could skip the global replace by doing `state mv` to a temp address and then `state mv` back after editing the temp tfstate's provider meta, but that's risky.
amal: @jack that'd be great, thanks. I'll wait and pair rather than doing global replace blind.
deploy-bot: CI: plan for branch `amal/fix-sp-import` ran and showed a lock held on the remote state for ~25s, automatically retried. Link: https://ci.local/plan/1234 :warning:
jack: TL;DR steps for pairing: 1) make a workspace backup (`terraform state pull > state.backup.json`), 2) try `terraform state replace-provider` in a local clone, 3) run `terraform plan` to confirm no recreate. If anything's off, restore from backup.
amal: Sounds good. I'll create a sandbox workspace and ping when ready. Thanks all :+1:
sanya: FYI, if this is a recurring issue for other identity imports we should add a quick checklist to the onboarding docs: "which provider alias to use when importing azuread vs azurerm resources".
amal: Good call — I'll drop a short note in docs after we resolve.
jack: Cool. ping me when you're in the sandbox and we can do steps together.
amal: Will do. Thanks everyone.
